subject: Peregrine Order Form — product title classification & training/feedback carveouts
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Subject: Peregrine: Order Form redlines — product title/training carveouts (attachments)

Hi all,

Quick context: Peregrine is ready to sign but their legal team pushed back on our proposed Order Form language around "productization" and training. They attached a legal redline (see Peregrine_OrderForm_Redline_v3.docx) and flagged MSA §7.2. Sales needs a firm, negotiable position by EOD Wednesday so we don't slip the closing window.

Ask for Legal (Laura): can you review the attached redlines and propose two alternatives we can offer Peregrine:
- Option A (customer-favorable): preserves customer output title but limits Redwood use to aggregated telemetry for safety only; no retraining on customer prompts/content.
- Option B (balanced): customer owns outputs; Redwood retains a non-exclusive, revocable feedback license to use anonymized/aggregated signals to improve models and safety, explicitly excluding model retraining on customer-provided content unless customer opts in via a separate agreement.

Operational note (Ben): if Option B is acceptable, what is the minimum telemetry retention/format we can provide for audits?

I'm looping in Marissa for customer coordination and timeline. Please call out any escalatable terms (audit rights, escrow asks, indemnity linkage).

Attachments: Peregrine_OrderForm_Redline_v3.docx, MSA_section-7.2_redline.pdf

Thanks,
Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Peregrine: Order Form redlines — product title/training carveouts

Thanks for the context — reviewed the redlines and Peregrine's comments on §7.2 (training/use). High level: Peregrine wants clean ownership of outputs and a hard bar on any use for model training. Their redline is stricter than we can accept without losing the ability to maintain model safety and shared improvements.

Suggested approach (deliverable: two short clause alternatives for insertion into the Order Form and MSA):

1) Order Form clause (Option A - customer-favorable)
"Customer shall retain all right, title, and interest in Outputs generated by the Service from Customer Content. Redwood may collect and retain non-identifying telemetry and aggregated usage statistics for the sole purpose of monitoring service performance and safety. Redwood shall not use Customer Content or Outputs to train or further develop any models or models weights without Customer's prior written consent."

2) Order Form clause (Option B - balanced compromise)
"Customer retains ownership of Outputs. Subject to strict de-identification, Redwood is granted a limited, non-exclusive, revocable license to use Aggregated and Anonymized Feedback derived from service usage for the sole purpose of improving Redwood's models, safety filters, and platform stability. Aggregated and Anonymized Feedback shall not include Customer Content or any Output in a form that is identifiable to Customer or individuals. Redwood shall not use raw Customer Content or non-deidentified Outputs to train models absent an explicit, opt-in agreement with Customer."

Notes / escalation flags:
- "Aggregated and Anonymized Feedback" needs a definition (examples: token-level counts, failure rates, safety filter triggers, prompt-surface statistics) — operationally we can provide dashboards and sample export formats.
- Audit requests: limited to 1x/year with 10 business days' notice; we can offer a redacted evidence package rather than full raw logs.
- Telemetry retention: propose default 90 days for per-request logs, 24 months for aggregated metrics; can negotiate longer retention for compliance customers with appropriate safeguards.
- If customer insists on zero use for any model improvement, route to GTM/Leadership for commercial offset (higher price or dedicated capacity).

I'll attach a marked PDF for MSA §7.2 language and a short rationale memo.

Proposed next step: Dylan to share both option snippets with Peregrine and ask which they prefer. If they counter with a narrower "no-train" ask, we'll need to escalate pricing/ops.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
Attachment: MSA_section-7.2_redline.pdf

Elena — forwarding our counsel's read and two workable clause options (attached). We want to get alignment on one of these so legal can prepare a clean Order Form.

Option A: Customer owns Outputs; Redwood cannot use Customer Content or Outputs for any model training.
Option B (preferred by Redwood): Customer owns Outputs; Redwood may use Aggregated and Anonymized Feedback for model safety and improvements but will not use raw Customer Content or identifiable Outputs for training without explicit opt-in.

Can you confirm which path Peregrine prefers? If neither, please send a marked counter with the minimum commercial ask you'd need to close (e.g., dedicated capacity, higher fee, telemetry carveout).

Also: what procurement timeline are we looking at? Marissa, any scheduling constraints?

Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Peregrine Order Form — product title classification & training/feedback carveouts

Dylan / Marissa,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the two clause choices. Our position from Legal/Procurement: we need clean ownership of Outputs (we'll use them for productization downstream). We're okay with Redwood collecting telemetry for uptime/incident purposes, but we cannot accept any clause that allows model retraining on customer content. Retraining is an unacceptable risk for us.

Proposed compromise (attached as Peregrine_requested_changes_20260406.pdf):
- Customer retains all Output title.
- Redwood may collect Aggregated Telemetry and Safety Signals but must ensure irreversible de-identification before use.
- Redwood shall not use Customer Content, Outputs, or de-identified derivatives for model retraining or to create model weights without a separately-negotiated agreement.
- Redwood to provide quarterly aggregate safety dashboards (no raw logs).
- Telemetry retention: 12 months for aggregated metrics; per-request logs only kept for 30 days for incident troubleshooting.
- Audit: one request per year for redacted evidence packages; no live access to raw data.

If Redwood needs the right to use anonymized signals for safety, we can consider a narrowly-scoped clause that excludes any text-level artifacts or examples and limits use to statistical metrics (failure rates, filter triggers, token-frequency histograms).

Procurement timeline: we are planning a purchase order in the next 10 business days if contract language is acceptable.

Tom Reed (cc'd) will handle the formal markups — if you can provide a clean Option B with the clarifying limits above, we can likely proceed.

Best,
Elena Morales
Head of Product, Peregrine Systems
Attachment: Peregrine_requested_changes_20260406.pdf

Subject: Re: Peregrine Order Form — product title classification & training/feedback carveouts

Elena / Tom,

Appreciate the clarity and the timeline — good news on the 10-business-day PO window. We reviewed your proposed carveout with Legal and Ops and believe we can meet in the middle. High-level proposal:

- Redwood will grant Customer ownership of Outputs in the Order Form (clear title language).
- Redwood will accept a prohibition on using Customer Content or Output for model "retraining" or creation of model weights absent an opt-in agreement.
- Redwood will retain the right to collect Aggregated and Irreversibly De-identified Feedback strictly limited to safety/quality improvements (examples: failure rates, classification accuracy by anonymized bucket, safety filter trigger counts). No text-level artifacts, no verbatim examples.
- Telemetry retention: we will adopt 12 months for aggregated metrics and 30 days for per-request logs for troubleshooting.
- Audit: Redwood will provide a redacted evidence package once per year (10 business days' notice). For compliance customers only, we can discuss extended retention and bespoke evidence packages under a separate SOW.

If that captures your ask, Laura will turn this into a clean Order Form addendum (Option B - customer output + limited feedback license) and we'll send it back for sign-off. Commercially: no immediate price change; if Peregrine later requests broader productization / redistribution rights we will need to revisit pricing.

Next steps:
1) Laura to prepare clean Order Form language and return by EOD Thursday.
2) Peregrine to confirm acceptance so Marissa can push procurement to issue PO within 10 business days.
